prompt: An empty junior planner chair sits at a dark workstation in a supply chain control room; a single overhead pendant lamp casts warm light from the left while cool cobalt monitor glow fills the right. rationale: Cinematic still suits a decisive place-and-shift story: the empty control-room seat is a scene, not an object study, and the anamorphic frame captures the tension between the absent junior bench and the persistent forecast screens. It avoids macro/product abstraction and places systemic abandonment in a physical operations environment.

core_thesis: Planning software is being funded out of the planner payroll, and the entry-level bench cut first is the same bench that learns when to overrule the forecast — so a 2.1-year deal outlives the judgment it depends on.
core_conflict: Subscription backlog growth versus payroll-driven entry-level headcount cuts, leaving software without the human judgment that must overrule forecasts.
